bundle.author: tomer-tgp
bundle.title: docs: say where agent experiment runs work
bundle.body:
A teammate setting up locally assumed a working Gemini key plus AWS credentials would let the community-issues research job run on a laptop, and that PR previews run it. Neither holds, and agents keep re-deriving this from deploy config.

- Local can't work even with credentials: a run's result comes back on dev's shared agent-results queue, dev gp-api consumes it, finds no matching row, and the local run sits `QUEUED`. So the answer is seed locally, not vend AWS creds.
- Previews have no `AGENT_DISPATCH_QUEUE_NAME` by design.
- `MEETINGS_AUTOMATION_ENABLED` is prod-only and gates only the on-create dispatch and crons, so on dev a real run needs the staff dispatch buttons or the dispatch endpoints.

The local setup guide gets the general rule; the communityIssues doc gets the per-environment detail and the manual triggers.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Documentation-only; no runtime, config, or deployment behavior changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Documents **where agent experiment runs actually work** so local/preview setup mistakes stop recurring.
> 
> **`docs/development.md`** adds a short callout that a local stack cannot run agent experiments (community issues, briefings, etc.): results land on dev’s shared queue and dev gp-api owns consumption, so extra `LOCAL_DEV_ENV` keys or AWS creds won’t help. It steers people to **seed locally** (e.g. `POST /v1/community-issues/seed`) and run real jobs on **dev**, notes **`MEETINGS_AUTOMATION_ENABLED` is prod-only** (dev won’t auto-dispatch gated flows), and that **PR previews** can’t run experiments—pointing to the community-issues agent doc for detail.
> 
> **`packages/gp-api/src/communityIssues/AGENTS.md`** adds a **“Where a real run works”** section: requirements (`AGENT_DISPATCH_QUEUE_NAME` + shared results queue), per-environment behavior (local → use `/seed`; preview → queue unset → `FAILED`; dev → manual staff/endpoint triggers), and why dev doesn’t auto-dispatch new offices without prod automation.
>

+A local stack can't run agent experiments (community issues, briefings,

 `meetingBriefings.service.ts` — the two domains use the same threshold and

+## Where a real run works
+
+A real run needs `AGENT_DISPATCH_QUEUE_NAME`, and its result returns on the
+env's shared agent-results queue (`src/agentExperiments/AGENTS.md`).
+
+- **Local:** no. Don't vend AWS credentials or point a laptop at
+  `agent-dispatch-dev.fifo`: dev gp-api consumes the result, finds no
+  matching run in its DB, and the local row stays `QUEUED`. Use
+  `POST /seed` for UI work.
+- **PR preview:** no. The queue is unset by design, so dispatch flips the row
+  to `FAILED`.
+- **Dev:** yes, but only when triggered by hand. `MEETINGS_AUTOMATION_ENABLED`
+  is `true` only in prod, and it gates only `onElectedOfficeCreated` and the
+  crons. So a new dev office dispatches nothing. Use the staff buttons on the
+  Serve Community Issues page (`POST /self-dispatch`, `@goodparty.org`
+  login), `POST /dispatch-if-needed`, or `POST /dispatch`.
+
